Round5 adds falsifiers and contribution evidence in docs/owned/p2r5-repairs.json without duplicating these IDs; the partial Japanese and future UI clauses below remain deferred to their phases.

partial.INV-PACK-08: HALF IMPLEMENTED, DELIBERATELY. The registry line has two clauses: (1) every accepted answer is in the unit's declared register, and (2) for Japanese every script variant (kanji+okurigana, all-kana, katakana) is enumerated as a set. Clause (1) is implemented here for SPANISH ONLY, as V6 with a marker table in config/g7.py::ES_REGISTER_MARKERS. Clause (2) is P7's: it needs the characters stage, JmdictFurigana and SudachiPy reading_form(), and EC-GRD-16 widens it to FOUR classes, not three — the alternate-okurigana headwords of the same JMdict entry (`引越し` for `引っ越し`, `落す` for `落とす`) are a fourth class the registry line does not name. Rather than half-implement it, V6 returns a BLOCKING finding for any language outside V6_IMPLEMENTED_LANGUAGES, so a Japanese pack cannot reach a pass through this validator at all. tests/falsifiers/INV-PACK-08.json carries a `japanese_half` block that exists to be refused, and test_INV_PACK_08_japanese_is_refused_not_passed asserts the refusal. The id should NOT be treated as fully green until P7 lands clause (2).

rulings.S043 Put the events in order: Out of v1 by founder ruling (no grading contract, no taxonomy home). Made unreachable, not merely unwritten: it has no row in config/g7.py::SHAPES, no member in config/base.py::EXERCISE_TYPES, and config/g7.py::FORBIDDEN_SHAPE_IDS names it so shapes.shape() and shapes.route() both raise ForbiddenShape carrying the ruling text rather than a KeyError that reads like a typo. test_g7_expand.py::test_S043_the_instruction_string_is_never_a_renderable_literal walks every module with ast and fails if the instruction ever appears as a non-docstring string literal — with its own falsifier, because a grep over the whole file would fail on the three modules that quote S043 while stating the ruling.
rulings.The distractor re-ranker: scope2/00 §2.3 puts an LLM on G7 as a RE-RANKER ONLY. No hosted model is reachable from this environment and no API key exists, so exercises/distractors.py::rerank() is declared with the contract a future implementation must satisfy (a permutation of the rule core's output, never a new candidate, so V5 stays true whatever the model says) and raises RerankerUnavailable. It has NO CALL SITE, and test_the_reranker_has_no_call_site walks the module with ast to prove it — because 'the hook is unimplemented' behind a false flag is still a call site somebody flips on. A heuristic wearing the re-ranker's name would put a claim in the pack manifest that is not true.
rulings.The alignment fallback is a declared eng: pyproject.toml's rule is that a stage which needs an absent dependency group fails loudly and never degrades to a worse tool. So DEFAULT_ALIGNMENT_ENGINE is `simalign` and an absent `align` group is exit 3 with `uv sync --group align`. CI does not carry torch, so CI reaches the deterministic aligner by NAMING it: `coursekit build es --only g7 --set align_engine=deterministic`. Whichever ran is written to the runlog entry as alignment_engine / alignment_quality / alignment_note, and the fallback's note says in as many words that a pack built with it must not ship. There is no `auto`.
rulings.meaning_select is dropped rather than ha: A newly introduced lexeme gets BOTH recognition forms or neither. If the alignment produced no gloss for the lemma, or there are not enough same-POS same-band glossed neighbours to fill the option list, stages/g7_expand.py::_lexeme_drafts returns nothing at all — because a lexeme item with one punitive form fails INV-PACK-07, and the word is still taught inside that lesson's sentence exercises. A lemma dropped this way is also not match-eligible, which falls out of _match_eligible_lemmas reading drafts rather than reading new_lemmas.
rulings.A match is five items' form, not one ite: S033 tags five lexemes. validators/exercise.py::item_keys files a record with no source_sentence_id under ONE KEY PER TAGGED LEMMA, so a five-pair match counts as a second form for each of its five lexemes. EC-MIS-04 names exactly this case ('the left-hand lexeme is the queued mistake'), and a composite key would have failed INV-PACK-07 for every match in every pack, for a reason that is not true. THE CONVERSE IS NOW ENFORCED TOO, because the first attempt only asserted it: a match is a SECOND form and never a FIRST, so stages/g7_expand.py::_match_eligible_lemmas reads the drafts that already exist and offers build_match_pairs only lemmas already carrying MIN_FORMS_PER_MISSABLE_ITEM punitive lexeme-keyed drafts. Without that rule the obvious way to make S033 ship — feed it every glossed lemma in the lesson — turns each of the five tagged lemmas into a single-form missable item and INV-PACK-07 fails.
rulings.type_the_word_ending is authored or drop: deep/00-PRODUCT-MAP §3.2 S039 obliges the pipeline to store a morphological segmentation per surface form. ending_split is that segmentation and it refuses in two named cases (a stem-changing verb, a surface equal to its lemma) rather than returning a character chop. A sentence with no segmentable token authors no ending drill; the skip is visible on the runlog as ending_drills_planned vs ending_drills_written, and it is safe for INV-PACK-07 because a grammar draft carries source_sentence_id and is filed under its sentence item. An AUTHORED G5 candidate never gets an ending drill at all: it has not been through G1, and inventing a lemma and a POS here would put a second analyser into the pipeline.

measurements.eng-spa alignment, hand-checked gold sam: NO eng-spa F1 IS PUBLISHED for SimAlign (deep/10 §S7 reports eng-fra .94, eng-ces .87, eng-deu .81, eng-ron .65, eng-fas .67, eng-hin .55 and nothing for spa or jpn). A 15-pair eng-spa gold sample was hand-aligned for this lane and lives in tools/coursekit/tests/test_alignment.py::GOLD, including the cases a positional heuristic gets wrong: pro-drop (`Vivo` <- `I live`), periphrastic negation (`I do not eat` -> `No como`) and a two-token courtesy (`please` -> `por favor`). Measured 2026-09-12, DeterministicAligner against that sample: precision .783, recall .711, F1 .745, micro-averaged over 76 hand-aligned pairs across 15 sentences. SimAlign itself was NOT measured — torch is not installed here — so that row of the table is a skipped test, not a number. The .745 is a REGRESSION FLOOR (FALLBACK_F1_FLOOR = 0.70), never a quality claim: the sample is 15 sentences of A1 fixture text, all with a length ratio under 2:1, which is the easiest case a positional aligner ever sees.
measurements.the fallback's real behaviour: Measured, and it is not restraint: inside the length-ratio gate the deterministic aligner emits EXACTLY min(len(source), len(target)) pairs whether or not it has any lexical evidence, because a proportional diagonal always scores 1.0 on position and the greedy always finds it. FALLBACK_MIN_SCORE alone never reduces the pair count — that was measured and the module docstring now says so. FALLBACK_MAX_LENGTH_RATIO = 2.0 is the only refusal it has, and it was added because the module's 'allowed to produce nothing' claim was otherwise false.
measurements.the reverse word bank, before and after: Measured on the committed fixture ledger with `coursekit build es --only g7 --set align_engine=deterministic`. BEFORE: prompt `Write this in English / La sopa está muy rica.`, accepted `The soup is very tasty.`, distractors ["aprendo", "está", "conocerte"] — three Spanish words in an English bank, one of them (`está`) a word of the displayed prompt. AFTER: distractors ["book", "has", "table"]. The run emits 32 records across all 17 P2 shapes (was 19 records across 16, with match_pairs missing).
measurements.what the alignment buys, as numbers: From the same run's runlog entry: alignment_engine=deterministic, alignment_quality=unmeasured, alignment_pairs_written=5 (the records whose shape declares needs_alignment), word_bank_hints=7, hinted_glosses=[casa, cuartos, libro, mesa, pan, parque, perro], ending_drills_planned=1, ending_drills_written=1. These replace the previous report's claim that hints and tile order 'reach the pack', which was false.

contractGapsFiledAsRequests: coursekit/artifacts.py::EXERCISE has no `shape` field and `additionalProperties: false`, so the sixteen product-map shapes are projected onto eight coarse EXERCISE_TYPES and the shape is recovered from (type, instruction line of prompt) by shapes.shape_of_record. Every draft round-trips under a 10,000-case property test, so nothing is lost today — but the player at P3 has to decode a prompt to know what to render. REQUEST: add `shape` (enum over config/g7.py::SHAPES ids) to the EXERCISE record. That file is the deps lane's and changing it moves contract_digest(), so it is a deliberate cross-lane change, not something to slip in.

The same record has no field for the NEW WORD pill, and no field for which alignment engine produced its `alignment` pairs. The pill clause of INV-PACK-50 is discharged instead by a structural fact (the pill-eligible shapes are a subset of the lexeme-quoting shapes, re-asserted on every routing decision by shapes.assert_pill_shapes_quote_lexemes), and the engine is written to the runlog. Both are sound; both would be simpler as fields.

config/base.py::VALIDATOR_IDS has no id for INV-PACK-07 or INV-PACK-50. They run as STAGE GATES inside G7 (the stage refuses to write an artefact that fails them) and as functions the tests call with the committed falsifiers. REQUEST: add `F6` (INV-PACK-07) and `F7` (INV-PACK-50) to VALIDATOR_IDS and VALIDATOR_TITLES so `coursekit validate` reports them on a pack it did not build itself.

config/g7.py::DEFAULT_REGISTER_BY_SLOT and REGISTERS resolve unit_assignment.register_slot to a concrete register. That mapping is arguably G3's (config/curriculum.py, which is empty and owned by p2-g3-curriculum). It lives here because V6 is the only consumer today; if G3 lands its own, the two must be reconciled into config/base.py rather than duplicated.

Registry.reset_for_tests() in coursekit/__init__.py clears the entries AND the discovered flag, but rediscovery calls importlib.import_module on modules already in sys.modules, so @register_stage never runs again. Any test using tests/conftest.py::empty_registry therefore unregisters every REAL stage for the rest of the pytest session, and the CLI then exits 2 for a stage that is plainly registered. This lane works around it with an autouse fixture in test_g7_expand.py that reloads the stage module; the fix belongs in Registry.reset_for_tests (re-run the decorators, or drop the modules from sys.modules) or in conftest, neither of which is this lane's file.

coursekit/artifacts.py::EXERCISE has no `tiles`, no `answer_indices` and no `hints`. The measured S035 mechanic is that the grid never reflows — tapping a tile leaves a blank placeholder in its original position — which needs a tile ORDER fixed for the session and a separate tile per repeated answer token. Today the pack ships the extra tiles plus the alignment and the player fixes the order once at session start (storing indices in session_state), which is sufficient but puts a build-time content decision in the runtime. REQUEST: add `word_bank: {tiles: [string], answer_indices: [int]}` and `hints: [{source_index, surface, gloss}]` to the EXERCISE record. Same file and same digest move as the `shape` request above, so the two should land together.

packages/core/src/journey/ownership.ts reads ONLY the `owned` array of every docs/owned/*.json and assumes (a) the id is in the P1 roster, (b) its owning test is a Vitest `it()` name, and (c) its falsifier is at packages/core/src/<module>/__falsifiers__/<id>.json. None of the three holds for a P2 pytest lane. REQUEST (integrate task, not this lane): a `phase` field honoured by p1Roster, a pytest test-name scan, and a falsifier search path that includes tools/coursekit/tests/falsifiers/. Until that lands, `owned` stays [] here.
falsifiers: tools/coursekit/tests/falsifiers/INV-PACK-07.json, INV-PACK-08.json, INV-PACK-50.json. Each carries a `falsifier` block that MUST fail, a `repair` block that MUST pass, and a third block for the subtler failure mode of the same invariant (a non-punitive second form; a mixed-register answer; a lexeme-quoting prompt quoting something outside the tag set). Every record in every block is validated against the frozen `exercise` schema on load, so a falsifier that drifts from the contract fails loudly instead of being rejected by the gate for the wrong reason.
whyOwnedIsEmpty: Not a deferral and not a gap: the tests exist, they carry the ids in their names, and they are driven by committed falsifier JSON with a must-fail and a must-pass block. What does not exist is a coverage map that can see a pytest name or a coursekit falsifier path. Listing the ids in `owned` before that lands does not make them covered; it makes four unrelated P1 gates fail, which is strictly worse than a gap somebody wrote down.

adversarialReviewRound2.$comment: Ten findings from the refuter that rejected the first attempt, and what each one cost. Every entry names the test that would now catch it.
adversarialReviewRound2.ownershipBrokeP1Gates: FIXED. `owned` is now [] with the ids in `ownedByPytest`; the two journey test files are green again on this branch.
adversarialReviewRound2.matchPairsNeverShipped: FIXED, but NOT the way the refuter suggested, and the difference matters. The suggestion was to feed `build_match_pairs` the lesson's glossed lemmas rather than only `new_lemmas`. That builds a match over lemmas with no other punitive lexeme form, and `validators/exercise.py::item_keys` files a match under ONE KEY PER TAGGED LEMMA — so each of those five lemmas becomes a SINGLE-FORM MISSABLE ITEM and INV-PACK-07 fails, in exactly the way this file's own ruling says it must not. What shipped instead: `_match_eligible_lemmas` reads the drafts that already exist and offers `build_match_pairs` only lemmas carrying MIN_FORMS_PER_MISSABLE_ITEM punitive lexeme-keyed drafts, and the test fixture was widened from one new lemma per lesson to seven so the shape is reachable at all. S033 is now emitted by a real run, with three tests over it (test_S033_match_pairs_is_emitted_by_a_real_run_with_five_rows, test_INV_PACK_07_a_match_is_only_built_over_lemmas_already_taught_twice, test_build_match_pairs_returns_none_below_five_glossed_rows).
adversarialReviewRound2.endToEndAssertionWasNarrowerThanTheClaim: FIXED. The end-to-end test now asserts the recognition row explicitly AND asserts SET EQUALITY between the shapes a real run emits and the P2-available rows of SHAPES, so 'every shape this phase ships' cannot drift from a hand-maintained list again. A real run emits all 17 P2 shapes.
adversarialReviewRound2.reverseWordBankShippedSpanishTiles: FIXED. `word_bank_reverse` now draws from `exercises/distractors.py::L1DecoyPool` — an English pool built from the sibling sentences' translations with every course-language lemma removed — and `_decoys` excludes every token of the displayed prompt in BOTH directions. Measured before: distractors ["aprendo", "está", "conocerte"] under the prompt `Write this in English / La sopa está muy rica.`. Measured after: ["book", "has", "table"]. Six tests in test_distractors.py plus test_the_reverse_word_bank_ships_english_tiles_not_course_language_ones and test_the_forward_word_bank_never_draws_a_decoy_from_its_own_prompt.
adversarialReviewRound2.alignmentAndHintsReachedNothing: HALF FIXED, HALF STATED PLAINLY, and the split is a contract limit rather than a choice. FIXED: every record whose shape declares `needs_alignment` now carries the pass-1 alignment pairs (measured: 5 of 32 records in the fixture run, and the misleading `_ = alignment` line is gone). STATED PLAINLY: the frozen `exercise` record has NO field for a tile list, an answer-index list or a hint list, and coursekit/artifacts.py is the deps lane's file, so the pack cannot ship them. What ships is the alignment the hints are derived from; `build_hints` now has a real call site in the stage and its output is written to the runlog as `word_bank_hints` (7 in the fixture run) and `hinted_glosses`, so a pack whose aligner produced no hintable token says so in a number instead of shipping a feature that renders nothing. wordbank.py's docstring no longer claims a pack without a tile order 'hands the player no way to keep the grid still' — the player fixes an order at session start and stores the indices in session_state, which is where stillness actually lives. The contract request for `tiles`, `answer_indices` and `hints` is in contractGapsFiledAsRequests.
adversarialReviewRound2.chatDistractorShippedCasefolded: FIXED. `AlternativesIndex` now keeps an `originals` map from the normalised comparison key back to the authored string, and `_chat_distractor` returns that. Measured before: `el pan está caliente.`; after: `El pan está caliente.`. test_the_complete_the_chat_distractor_is_a_verbatim_ledger_sentence asserts the distractor is verbatim in the ledger and starts with a capital; test_the_alternatives_index_renders_the_authored_casing asserts the index itself.
adversarialReviewRound2.wordEndingWasACharacterChop: FIXED, not deferred. `stages/g7_expand.py::ending_split` is a real per-surface-form segmentation with two rules and two refusals: a regular verb's stem is its infinitive minus the two-letter ending (correr -> corr + e, estar -> est + á) and a stem-changing form gets NOTHING (tener -> ten, surface `tiene`, no split); everything else splits at the longest common prefix with its own lemma (cuartos -> cuarto + s, rica -> ric + a) and a citation form (caliente) has no ending. Guarded by MIN_ENDING_STEM_CHARS=2 and MAX_ENDING_CHARS=4. Measured before: `El pan está calien____` -> `te`. After: `El pan est____ caliente` -> `á`. A sentence with no segmentable token authors no drill at all and the skip is on the runlog (`ending_drills_planned` vs `ending_drills_written`); that is safe for INV-PACK-07 because a grammar draft carries `source_sentence_id` and is filed under its sentence item, whose SENTENCE_FORM_PLAN row already carries two punitive forms. 11 parametrised cases plus three tests.
adversarialReviewRound2.v6FalsePositiveOnThirdPersonSpanish: FIXED. `le`, `les`, `su`, `sus`, `suyo`, `suya`, `suyos`, `suyas` and `consigo` are removed from ES_REGISTER_MARKERS['usted'] and kept as ES_AMBIGUOUS_THIRD_PERSON_FORMS so the regression has something to assert against. They are the ordinary third-person clitic, possessive and reflexive and carry no register; with them listed, `A él le gusta su casa.` was reported as a BLOCKING 'mixes registers' finding in a tuteo unit, i.e. any A1 Spanish pack containing `su casa` or `le gusta` was unshippable. test_register_of_is_lexical_and_accent_insensitive was asserting the wrong behaviour and now asserts {'tu'}; two new tests carry INV-PACK-08 (test_INV_PACK_08_ordinary_third_person_spanish_carries_no_register with the exact regression case the refuter named, and test_INV_PACK_08_a_third_person_answer_passes_v6_in_a_tu_unit). The `mixed_register` block of tests/falsifiers/INV-PACK-08.json depended on the bug — its answer was `Tu casa es su casa.` — and is now `Tu casa es la casa de usted.`, which mixes registers for real. SECOND BUG FOUND WHILE FIXING IT: `validators/exercise.py::_words` replaced only `¿` and `?`, so a marker at the END of a sentence was read as `usted.` and matched nothing — V6 silently missed every out-of-register answer that put the pronoun last, which in Spanish is where it usually goes. It now strips by Unicode category.
adversarialReviewRound2.propertyRunsDownscale: FIXED, not recorded. tests/test_distractors.py::test_V5_the_rule_core_never_returns_a_valid_alternative runs the full PROPERTY_RUNS (10,000) like the other two, not PROPERTY_RUNS // 10. No property in this lane is below the plan's floor.
adversarialReviewRound2.staleJsEvidence: The previous report cited /tmp/g7-js.log, which was written BEFORE docs/owned/p2-g7.json existed and which itself ended non-zero. The report for this round cites a JS run made on the final committed tree and names its exit code.

$ownedAtIntegration: Added at P2 integration. The lane wrote the owning tests and left the ids unclaimed because on its own branch the coverage map could not see a pytest claim at all — `scripts/coverage-map.ts` walked only packages/apps/e2e, and the two Python claim conventions were each readable by one lane's scanner. Both readers are now unioned in scripts/coverage-map.ts and packages/core/src/journey/ownership.ts, so the claim is load-bearing: delete a test and CI goes red.
